AI Guardrail Selection & Confused Deputy FAQ: Model-Level Shields vs. Zero-Trust Capability Broker
First-Principles Guide: Why Shared API Keys & Prompt Classifiers Fail on Indirect Injection, and How a 0.0199ms Broker Enforces 0% ASR
🎯 Q1 · Architect Selection Rule: Model-Level Guardrails (Option A) vs. Zero-Trust Broker (Option B)
1. When to choose Option A (Model-Level Content Guardrails: Azure Prompt Shields / LlamaFirewall)?
Best for read-only Q&A chatbots & public RAG (zero write/email/payment tools), or as a Layer-1 ingress pre-filter (drops 70%–85% obvious jailbreaks).
2. Why standalone Model Guardrails fail once Agents have Tools / MCP (25.0%–42.9% Bypass Rate)
Indirect instructions inside vendor invoices look like polite business prose (zero hacker keywords), and multi-hop/cipher splits blind text classifiers.
3. When you MUST enforce Option B (Deterministic Zero-Trust Capability Broker)?
Rule: Any agent with restricted DB reads, external messaging, MCP tools, or payments must enforce provenance + taint IFC + 5-tuple HITL at the tool gate.
🔍 Q2 & Q3 · First Principles: What is a "Confused Deputy" & How 4 Locks Stop It in 0.0199ms
Inside an LLM, instructions and untrusted data share one token window with zero grammar boundary.
Architectural Fix: Move enforcement out of the LLM's probabilistic brain and into a 0.0199ms Deterministic Capability Broker!
📊 Architect Decision Matrix (Four Guardrail Architectures Head-to-Head)
Hardened Zero-Trust Capability Broker (0.0% ASR · -75 pts)
☑ 1. Eliminate shared API keys; pin original_requester
☑ 2. Enforce context_labels taint; block tainted egress
☑ 4. Bind HITL approvals to 5-tuple hash & run epoch
☑ 6. Pin AgBOM SHA-256 hashes & audit server receipts
